newsitem.title: CANADA: CanAmera crushing plant open after two deaths.
newsitem.headline: CanAmera crushing plant open after two deaths.

text.p: CanAmera Foods' canola crushing plant in Altona, Man., continued operating on Friday after two workers were killed and one was injured on Thursday, CanAmera vice-president Herb Schafer told Reuters.
"The crushing plant is operating right now, but at this point that's all I can talk about right now because the accident's still under investigation," Schafer said.
A 41-year-old man was in critical condition at a Winnipeg hospital following the accident early Thursday afternoon that left two other men dead, Altona police said.
The dead men were found in a railway tanker, police said.
CanAmera is 50 percent owned by Saskatchewan Wheat Pool, Manitoba Pool Elevators and 50 percent owned by Central Soya, which itself is owned by private French company Eridania Begain-Say.
